questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under RBI's directions of 10 October 2026 on foreign exchange derivative contracts involving the INR, what is the new threshold for the facilities that let users undertake such transactions without establishing underlying exposure?

options.text: USD 100 million equivalent of notional value outstanding at any time
USD 5 million equivalent of notional value outstanding at any time
USD 2 million equivalent per transaction
USD 25 million equivalent per financial year

solution.explanation: The 10 October 2026 directions cut the threshold for these facilities from USD 100 million to USD 5 million equivalent of notional value outstanding at any time. Users must give an undertaking that the same exposure is not hedged elsewhere, and ADs must keep documents for at least two years.
steps: New threshold: USD 5 million (outstanding at any time)
solution.why_others_wrong: USD 100 million was the earlier limit; USD 2 million is the threshold used for the Foreign Exchange Risk Reserve; USD 25 million per year is not prescribed.
solution.final_answer: Option B: USD 5 million equivalent of notional value outstanding at any time

fact_checks.claim: 'The threshold for each of the above facilities shall, henceforth, be USD 5 million equivalent of notional value (outstanding at any point of time)'; the earlier limit for positions without proving underlying exposure was USD 100 million.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: RBI's Commercial Banks – Minimum Capital Requirements for Market Risk Directions, 2026, issued on 21 September 2026, require banks to compute market-risk RWAs using which approach, and from when?

options.text: The internal models approach, from 1 October 2026
The basic indicator approach, from 1 April 2027
The simplified standardised approach, from 1 April 2027
The advanced measurement approach, from 1 January 2027

solution.explanation: The Directions require banks to use the simplified standardised approach (SSA) for market risk, with capital charges for interest rate, equity, foreign exchange and options risk, and replace the market risk section of the 2025 capital adequacy directions from 1 April 2027.
solution.why_others_wrong: No internal models approach is provided; the basic indicator and advanced measurement approaches belong to operational risk, not market risk.
solution.final_answer: Option C: The simplified standardised approach, from 1 April 2027

fact_checks.claim: 'A bank shall use the simplified standardised approach (SSA) for computing risk-weighted assets for market risk.' 'These Directions shall come into effect from April 1, 2027.'

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about RBI's Market Risk Directions, 2026 (21 September 2026):
I. They apply to all banking companies, including small finance banks, payments banks and local area banks.
II. The trading book includes all instruments classified as 'Held for Trading' under RBI's investment portfolio directions.
III. On their implementation, the section on 'Capital charge for market risk' in the 2025 capital adequacy directions (except one sub-section) stands repealed.
Which of the above is/are correct?

options.text: I and II only
II and III only
I and III only
I, II and III

solution.concept: Scope of the market risk directions
solution.explanation: 'Commercial Banks' here means banking companies other than SFBs, payments banks and local area banks, plus nationalised banks and SBI, so statement I is wrong. The trading book is all HFT instruments, with everything else in the banking book, and Section D (except D.8) on market risk in the 2025 capital adequacy directions is repealed.
steps: I: SFBs, PBs and LABs are excluded → wrong
III: Section D (except D.8) repealed → correct
solution.why_others_wrong: Statement I is wrong, so every option containing I is wrong.
solution.final_answer: Option B: II and III only

fact_checks.claim: 'Commercial Banks' means banking companies (other than Small Finance Banks, Payments Banks, and Local Area Banks), corresponding new banks, and the State Bank of India.

The trading book 'shall include all instruments classified as 'Held for Trading''; and 'Section D (except sub-section D.8) on 'Capital charge for market risk'' of the 2025 Capital Adequacy Directions 'shall stand repealed.'

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about RBI's Master Circular on credit facilities to Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (1 October 2026):
I. Under DAY-NRLM, 50% of the beneficiaries are to be SCs/STs.
II. Guarantee cover under the Credit Enhancement Guarantee Scheme for Scheduled Castes ranges from ₹0.15 crore to ₹5 crore, with IFCI Ltd as nodal agency.
III. Banks should review measures to improve credit flow to SC/ST borrowers on a half-yearly basis.
Which of the above is/are correct?

options.text: I and II only
II and III only
I and III only
I, II and III

solution.explanation: The master circular consolidates 21 earlier circulars. It records that DAY-NRLM aims for 50% SC/ST beneficiaries, that at least 40% of DRI advances go to SC/ST borrowers, and that CEGSSC cover ranges from ₹0.15 crore to ₹5 crore with IFCI as nodal agency. Banks must review the measures quarterly, not half-yearly.
solution.why_others_wrong: Statement III is wrong, so options containing III are wrong.
solution.final_answer: Option A: I and II only

fact_checks.claim: DAY-NRLM would ensure coverage 'such that 50% of these beneficiaries are SCs/STs'; 'The amount of guarantee cover under CEGSSC ranges from a minimum of ₹0.15 cr to a maximum of ₹5.00 cr.' 'IFCI Ltd. has been designated as the Nodal Agency under the scheme.'
'Banks should review the measures taken to enhance the flow of credit to SC/ST borrowers on a quarterly basis.'

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: According to RBI's Digital Rupee (e₹) FAQs, what fees or charges does a user pay for holding and using a retail e₹ wallet?

options.text: A flat annual wallet maintenance fee fixed by RBI
A small charge on every person-to-merchant payment
A charge only when e₹ is redeemed back to the bank account
None; no fees or charges apply to e₹ or e₹ wallets

solution.concept: Charges on the retail digital rupee
solution.explanation: RBI's e₹ FAQs state that no fees or charges apply to e₹ or to e₹ wallets. Like cash, the digital rupee can be loaded, spent and redeemed without a charge to the user.
steps: Recall RBI's FAQ on fees for e₹
solution.why_others_wrong: RBI prescribes no wallet maintenance fee, no per-payment charge and no redemption charge for e₹; all three distractors invent charges the FAQ rules out.
solution.final_answer: Option D: None; no fees or charges apply to e₹ or e₹ wallets

fact_checks.claim: Are there fees? No fees or charges apply to e₹ or e₹ wallets.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: According to RBI's Digital Rupee FAQs, under which provision is every e₹ note legal tender anywhere in India, guaranteed by the Central Government?

options.text: Section 22 of the RBI Act, 1934
Section 10 of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007
Section 26 of the RBI Act, 1934
Section 6 of the Coinage Act, 2011

solution.explanation: RBI's FAQs say that under Section 26 of the RBI Act, 1934, every e₹ note is legal tender anywhere in India and is guaranteed by the Central Government. Being a digital form of the rupee note, e₹ is a liability of the RBI, just like a physical banknote.
steps: e₹ is a digital form of the banknote
Banknotes are legal tender under Section 26 of the RBI Act
solution.why_others_wrong: Section 22 gives RBI the sole right to issue banknotes but is not the legal-tender clause; the PSS Act governs payment systems, not legal tender; and the Coinage Act covers coins, not e₹ notes.
solution.final_answer: Option C: Section 26 of the RBI Act, 1934

fact_checks.claim: Under Section 26 of the RBI Act, 1934, every e₹ note is legal tender anywhere in India and is guaranteed by the Central Government. As a digital form of the ₹ note, it is a liability of the RBI.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A bank lets customers check balances and transfer funds by dialling a USSD code on a basic phone. Under RBI's Commercial Banks – Digital Banking Channels Authorisation Directions, 2025, this service falls under which channel?

options.text: Internet banking, which covers all channels that use a telecom network
A separate 'assisted banking' channel outside digital banking
Phone banking, which is not regulated by these Directions
Mobile banking, which covers mobile applications, USSD and SMS

solution.concept: Internet banking vs mobile banking under the 2025 Directions
solution.explanation: The Directions define mobile banking as a channel using mobile applications, USSD and SMS. Internet banking means operating accounts over the internet, including browser-based applications but excluding mobile applications. So a USSD service is mobile banking.
steps: Mobile banking = mobile apps, USSD and SMS
solution.why_others_wrong: Internet banking is browser-based and excludes mobile apps, so it does not cover USSD; the Directions create no separate assisted or phone-banking category for USSD.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Mobile banking, which covers mobile applications, USSD and SMS

fact_checks.claim: Internet banking: a channel for operating accounts over the internet, including browser-based applications but excluding mobile applications. Mobile banking: a channel using mobile applications, USSD, and SMS.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A bank wants to show an insurance company's products on its mobile banking app after the customer logs in. Under RBI's Commercial Banks – Digital Banking Channels Authorisation Directions, 2025, what is the position?

options.text: The bank may display them freely if the customer has given SMS consent
Third-party products shall not be displayed after login unless RBI permits it under the applicable Directions
They may be displayed only before login, on the app's landing page, without restriction
They may be displayed after login if the bank charges no fee for the display

solution.concept: Third-party products on digital banking channels
solution.explanation: The Directions say that after login, third-party products and services shall not be displayed on the bank's digital channels unless RBI permits it, as provided in the Undertaking of Financial Services Directions, 2025. Consent or a zero fee does not override this.
steps: Identify the rule on third-party products after login
Not displayed unless permitted by RBI
solution.why_others_wrong: Customer consent, a no-fee display or pre-login placement are not conditions the Directions recognise; the test is RBI permission under the Undertaking of Financial Services Directions.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Third-party products shall not be displayed after login unless RBI permits it under the applicable Directions

fact_checks.claim: After login, third-party products and services "shall not be displayed" on bank channels unless the RBI permits, per paras 58 to 62 of the Undertaking of Financial Services Directions, 2025.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A borrower complains to a bank about a loan taken through its digital lending app. Under the RBI (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025, when can the borrower take the complaint to RBI's Integrated Ombudsman Scheme?

options.text: If the complaint is rejected or he is dissatisfied, or he gets no reply within 30 days of its receipt by the lender
Only after 60 days, and only if the lending service provider has also rejected it
Immediately, since digital lending complaints go straight to RBI
Only after the lending service provider's nodal officer closes the complaint

solution.explanation: Lenders and their LSPs must designate nodal grievance redressal officers, but the responsibility for redressal remains with the regulated entity (lender). If the complaint is rejected wholly or partly, the borrower is dissatisfied, or there is no reply within 30 days of receipt by the lender, the borrower can complain under the RB-IOS through the CMS portal.
steps: Escalate if rejected/dissatisfied/no reply in 30 days
File under RB-IOS on the CMS portal
solution.why_others_wrong: The period is 30 days, not 60; the complaint must first go to the lender, not straight to RBI; and the LSP's officer cannot hold up escalation because responsibility stays with the lender.
solution.final_answer: Option A: If the complaint is rejected or he is dissatisfied, or he gets no reply within 30 days of its receipt by the lender

fact_checks.claim: Borrowers may escalate if a complaint is rejected in whole or part, they are dissatisfied, or they receive no reply "within 30 days of receipt of complaint by the RE".
"responsibility of grievance redressal shall continue to remain with the RE"

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under the RBI (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025, how must repayments of a digital loan flow, and what applies when a delinquent borrower repays in cash?

options.text: Repayments may pass through the LSP's pool account; cash recoveries are credited within 7 days
Repayments go to an escrow account of the LSP; cash recoveries are not allowed at all
Repayments go directly to the lender's account with no third-party pool account; a cash recovery must be reflected in the borrower's account the same day
Repayments may go to any account the borrower chooses; cash recoveries are credited at month-end

solution.explanation: The Directions require repayments to go directly to the regulated entity's account, without any pass-through or pool account of a third party, and bar third parties such as LSPs from controlling the fund flow. Cash recoveries from delinquent loans are allowed, but must be fully reflected in the borrower's account on the same day.
steps: Cash recovery: allowed, reflected the same day
solution.why_others_wrong: Pass-through, pool or escrow accounts of the LSP are prohibited; cash recovery is permitted, not barred; and the same-day rule rules out 7-day or month-end credit.
solution.final_answer: Option C: Repayments go directly to the lender's account with no third-party pool account; a cash recovery must be reflected in the borrower's account the same day

fact_checks.claim: Repayments go directly to the RE's account, with no "pass-through account/ pool account of any third party".
Cash recoveries on delinquent loans are permitted but must be fully reflected in the borrower's account the same day.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about RBI's Commercial Banks – Digital Banking Channels Authorisation Directions, 2025:
I. They came into effect from 1 January 2026.
II. To get approval for a transactional facility, a bank must have had no major adverse observations in its IS Audit reports for the last three financial years.
III. Where transaction limits under RBI instructions and payment network rules differ, the stricter of the two applies.
Which of the above is/are correct?

options.text: I and III only
I and II only
II and III only
I, II and III

solution.concept: Eligibility and risk controls for digital banking channels
solution.explanation: The Directions came into effect on 1 January 2026. A satisfactory compliance record for a transactional facility is judged through a GAICA report by a CERT-In empanelled auditor, no major adverse observations in IS Audit reports for the last two (not three) financial years, and supervisory inputs. Banks must set per-transaction, daily, weekly and monthly limits, and the stricter of RBI's and the payment network's requirements applies.
steps: II: the look-back is two financial years - wrong
III: stricter of the two applies - correct
solution.why_others_wrong: Any option containing II is wrong because the IS Audit look-back is two years; 'I and II only' also drops the correct statement III.
solution.final_answer: Option A: I and III only

fact_checks.claim: "These Directions shall come into effect from January 01, 2026."

A satisfactory compliance record, assessed through a CERT-In empanelled auditor's GAICA report, no major adverse observations in IS Audit reports for the last two financial years, and supervisory inputs.
Where RBI or payment network rules differ, "the requirements that are stricter of the two shall be applicable."

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under NPCI's directions to issuer banks, what happens to the balance in a UPI Lite account that has had no transaction for six months?

options.text: It is forfeited and credited to the DEA Fund
It is frozen until the user completes fresh KYC
It is converted into retail e₹ in the user's wallet
It is refunded to the user's source bank account

solution.explanation: NPCI directed issuer banks to identify 'zero transaction' UPI Lite accounts, those with no transaction in six months, and refund the amount lying in them to the source bank accounts. The money thus goes back to the user's own account.
steps: Inactive = no transaction in six months
Balance refunded to the source bank account
solution.why_others_wrong: The balance is not forfeited to the DEA Fund, not frozen pending KYC and not converted into e₹; NPCI requires a refund to the linked bank account.
solution.final_answer: Option D: It is refunded to the user's source bank account

fact_checks.claim: NPCI directed issuer banks to "identify zero transaction UPI Lite accounts and refund the amount lying in these accounts to the source bank accounts." Such accounts are those with "no transaction in six months."

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: According to NPCI's February 2025 circular on UPI Lite (to be implemented by 31 March 2025), what new facility did users get?

options.text: Payments of up to ₹5,000 at a time without a UPI PIN
'Transfer out', to move the UPI Lite balance back to the bank account without closing the wallet
Use of UPI Lite for international merchant payments
Interest on the UPI Lite balance at the savings rate

solution.explanation: NPCI's circular of 21 February 2025 asked members to provide a 'transfer out' facility so that users can withdraw funds from the UPI Lite balance to their bank account. Earlier, transfer out was possible only when the UPI Lite wallet was closed or disabled.
steps: Earlier: transfer out only on closing/disabling the wallet
Now: transfer out at any time to the bank account
solution.why_others_wrong: ₹5,000 is the overall UPI Lite limit, not the per-payment limit (₹1,000); the circular is not about international use; and UPI Lite balances earn no interest.
solution.final_answer: Option B: 'Transfer out', to move the UPI Lite balance back to the bank account without closing the wallet

fact_checks.claim: "Under this facility, users will be able to withdraw funds from their UPI Lite wallet balance to their bank account" ... "Earlier transfer out was possible only when closing or disabling the UPI Lite wallet." Members to make changes "by March 31, 2025."

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under NPCI's circular of 27 February 2025 that raised the UPI Lite limits, how can a user replenish (top up) the used UPI Lite limit?

options.text: Only in online mode, with an additional factor of authentication (AFA)
Only offline, by tapping the phone at an NFC terminal
Only at a bank branch, by filling a top-up form
Automatically from any wallet, without any authentication

solution.explanation: While UPI Lite payments themselves are small and need no PIN, NPCI's circular says replenishment of the used limit is allowed only in online mode with an additional factor of authentication. This keeps the movement of money from the bank account into UPI Lite secure.
steps: Small payments from UPI Lite: no PIN
Top-up from the bank account: online with AFA
solution.why_others_wrong: Top-up is not done offline at NFC terminals or through branch forms, and it is never without authentication.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Only in online mode, with an additional factor of authentication (AFA)

fact_checks.claim: "Replenishment of the used limit shall be allowed only in online mode with AFA" ... "the enhanced limit shall be Rs 1000 per transaction with Rs 5,000 being the total limit."

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A cross-border link that went live on 6 June 2026 lets people in India and Nepal send money to each other in real time. It connects UPI with which Nepali system, and who built it?

options.text: Nepal's Fonepay network; built by NPCI and Nepal Rastra Bank
Nepal's National Payments Interface (NPI); built by SBI and Nepal SBI Bank Ltd
Nepal's National Payments Interface (NPI); built by NIPL and Nepal Clearing House Ltd
Nepal's NEFT-linked remittance scheme; built by RBI and Nepal Clearing House Ltd

solution.explanation: The UPI–NPI linkage connects India's UPI with Nepal's National Payments Interface. It was developed by NPCI International Payments Ltd (NIPL), NPCI's international arm, and Nepal Clearing House Ltd (NCHL), and became operational on 6 June 2026 for real-time peer-to-peer transfers both ways.
solution.why_others_wrong: Fonepay is a different Nepali network and the builders were not NPCI with Nepal Rastra Bank; SBI and Nepal SBI Bank run the older Indo-Nepal Remittance Facility, which uses NEFT, not this UPI link.
solution.final_answer: Option C: Nepal's National Payments Interface (NPI); built by NIPL and Nepal Clearing House Ltd

fact_checks.claim: The service became operational on "June 6, 2026" ... It connects India's UPI with Nepal's National Payments Interface (NPI) ... built by NPCI International Payments Limited (NIPL) ... and Nepal Clearing House Limited (NCHL).

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about the debate on charges on UPI in August 2026:
I. UPI has remained free for users and merchants since January 2020.
II. The Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026 amends Section 10A of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007, which the Ministry of Finance called only an enabling provision.
III. Once the Bill is enacted, RBI's Board for Regulation and Supervision of Payment and Settlement Systems will fix the MDR on UPI.
Which of the above is/are correct?

options.text: II and III only
I and II only
I and III only
I, II and III

solution.concept: Zero MDR on UPI and the 2026 amendment
solution.explanation: UPI has been free for users and merchants since January 2020. The Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026 amends Section 10A of the PSS Act so that the Centre can notify payment modes; the Ministry of Finance clarified on 8 August 2026 that this is only an enabling provision. questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: NEFT is available round the clock on all days and settles in half-hourly batches. According to RBI's NEFT FAQs, what happens if the NEFT system is not available at some time?

options.text: Pending transactions are automatically moved to RTGS
Banks must convert pending transfers into demand drafts
NPCI routes the pending transactions through IMPS
RBI broadcasts a message to all NEFT participants

solution.explanation: RBI's FAQs say NEFT is available on a 24x7x365 basis with batches every half hour. If the system is unavailable for any reason, RBI broadcasts a message to all participants of NEFT.
steps: Unavailability is announced by an RBI broadcast message
solution.why_others_wrong: There is no automatic shift of NEFT transactions to RTGS or IMPS, and no conversion into demand drafts; NEFT is operated by RBI, not NPCI.
solution.final_answer: Option D: RBI broadcasts a message to all NEFT participants

fact_checks.claim: "The NEFT system is available round the clock throughout the year on all days, i.e., on 24x7x365 basis." NEFT runs in batches every half hour. If it is unavailable, RBI broadcasts a message to all participants.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: An NEFT transfer is settled in the 15:30 batch, but the beneficiary's account turns out to be closed. According to RBI's NEFT FAQs, what must happen?

options.text: The beneficiary bank returns it by 17:30, and the originating bank shows the entry as 'NEFT-Return' in the remitter's statement
The beneficiary bank returns it by the end of the next working day, marked 'Unpaid NEFT'
The beneficiary bank holds the funds until the remitter files a claim with RBI
The beneficiary bank returns it within 30 minutes, marked 'NEFT-Reject'

solution.explanation: If the beneficiary's account cannot be credited, the destination bank must return the transaction to the originating branch within two hours of completion of the batch in which it was processed, here by 17:30. The originating bank should then mark the returned entry as 'NEFT-Return' in the remitter's pass book or statement.
solution.why_others_wrong: The return window is two hours from the batch, not the next working day and not 30 minutes (that is RTGS crediting); the bank cannot hold funds pending a claim; and the labels 'Unpaid NEFT' and 'NEFT-Reject' are not the prescribed one.
solution.final_answer: Option A: The beneficiary bank returns it by 17:30, and the originating bank shows the entry as 'NEFT-Return' in the remitter's statement

fact_checks.claim: The destination bank must "return the transaction (to the originating branch) within two hours of completion of the batch in which the transaction was processed."
If a payment fails, the originating bank should label the originator's entry "NEFT-Return" in the passbook or statement.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about RBI's circular of 6 December 2019 that made NEFT available 24x7 from 16 December 2019:
I. NEFT transactions after usual banking hours were expected to be automated transactions initiated through straight-through processing (STP) modes.
II. Member banks were expected to keep adequate liquidity in their current accounts with RBI at all times.
III. Banks were to send the positive confirmation message (N06) for all NEFT credits.
Which of the above is/are correct?

options.text: II and III only
I and III only
I and II only
I, II and III

solution.explanation: The 2019 circular said NEFT transactions after usual banking hours were expected to be automated, initiated through STP modes, and that member banks must keep adequate liquidity in their current accounts with RBI at all times so that every batch settles. It required positive confirmation for all NEFT credits through the N10 message, not N06.
steps: I: STP after banking hours - correct
II: adequate liquidity in RBI current account - correct
III: the positive confirmation message is N10 - wrong
solution.why_others_wrong: Options containing III are wrong because the message type is N10; 'I and III' and 'II and III' also leave out a correct statement.
solution.final_answer: Option C: I and II only

"Member banks are expected to keep adequate liquidity in their current account with Reserve Bank of India at all times"
"Member banks will ensure sending of positive confirmation message (N10) for all NEFT credits."

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: According to RBI's RTGS FAQs (updated October 2026), roughly how many bank branches are RTGS-enabled?

options.text: About 50,000
About 95,000
More than 5,00,000
More than 1,82,000

solution.explanation: Both the sending and the receiving branch must be RTGS-enabled. RBI's FAQs say more than 1,82,000 bank branches are RTGS-enabled, and the list is on RBI's website, updated every fortnight.
steps: Recall RBI's FAQ on RTGS-enabled branches
solution.why_others_wrong: 50,000 and 95,000 understate the network, and 5,00,000 exceeds the total number of bank branches in India.
solution.final_answer: Option D: More than 1,82,000

fact_checks.claim: Both the sending and receiving branches must be RTGS-enabled. More than 1,82,000 branches are enabled. RBI's website lists them, updated every fortnight.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: In RTGS the beneficiary bank credits the account solely on the basis of the account number in the payment message. What reason do RBI's RTGS FAQs give for this?

options.text: The beneficiary's name is not allowed to be part of an RTGS message
Names cannot be matched before credit in a real-time system, and spellings of names vary in India
RBI's books record only account numbers, not names
The name check is done afterwards by NPCI for all RTGS credits

solution.concept: Credit on account number in RTGS
solution.explanation: RBI explains that in a real-time transfer, matching names before crediting is not possible, and the spelling of names varies across India. Credit is therefore given on the account number alone, which is why the remitter must be extremely careful with it.
steps: Real-time credit leaves no time for name matching
Hence credit on account number only
solution.why_others_wrong: The beneficiary's name is a required field in an RTGS message; RBI's books hold banks' settlement accounts, not customer names; and NPCI does no after-the-fact name check of RTGS credits.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Names cannot be matched before credit in a real-time system, and spellings of names vary in India

fact_checks.claim: Real-time transfers can't match names before crediting, and name spellings vary in India. Chapter 11 of the RTGS System Regulations has more detail.
Be extremely careful with the account number, since credit depends only on it.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A new entity has applied for membership of the RTGS system. According to RBI's RTGS FAQs, where is the membership procedure laid down, and how can the applicant check the status of its application?

options.text: In the RTGS System Regulations; the status can be checked on RBI's PRAVAAH portal
In the NPCI Procedural Guidelines; the status can be checked on the NPCI website
In the Banking Regulation Act, 1949; the status is sent by post
In the RBI Act, 1934; the status can be checked on the CIMS portal

solution.explanation: RBI's FAQs say the procedure for RTGS membership is set out in the RTGS System Regulations, and applicants can check the status of their application through the PRAVAAH portal. Timelines for applications under the PSS Act, 2007 are set in RBI's Citizens' Charter.
solution.why_others_wrong: RTGS is owned and run by RBI, not NPCI; the BR Act and RBI Act do not lay down RTGS membership procedure; and CIMS is RBI's supervisory returns portal, not the application-tracking portal.
solution.final_answer: Option A: In the RTGS System Regulations; the status can be checked on RBI's PRAVAAH portal

fact_checks.claim: How do entities apply for membership? The procedure is set out in the RTGS System Regulations. How can applicants check their status? Through the PRAVAAH portal.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements based on RBI's RTGS FAQs:
I. Unlike NEFT, which settles transactions in batches, RTGS processes each transaction continuously throughout the day.
II. Customers can track the status of an RTGS transaction directly in the RTGS system.
III. The lists of IFSCs and RTGS-enabled branches on RBI's website are updated every fortnight.
Which of the above is/are correct?

options.text: I and II only
I and III only
II and III only
I, II and III

solution.explanation: RTGS processes instructions continuously, while NEFT batches transactions received up to set times. Customers cannot track an RTGS transaction themselves; under positive confirmation the remitting bank gets the credit confirmation and informs them. RBI's IFSC and branch lists are updated every fortnight.
steps: II: customers cannot track directly - wrong
solution.why_others_wrong: Options containing II are wrong because RBI says customers cannot track RTGS directly; 'I and II only' also omits the correct statement III.
solution.final_answer: Option B: I and III only

fact_checks.claim: NEFT batches transactions received up to set times. RTGS processes each transaction continuously throughout the day.
Customers cannot track it directly. Under positive confirmation, the remitting bank receives RBI's confirmation, via the beneficiary bank, that the money was credited, and then informs the customer.
RBI's website publishes IFSC lists, updated every fortnight.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
At 21:00 on a Sunday, Alpha Traders sends ₹30 lakh by RTGS to Beta Ltd. Beta's bank receives the payment message at 21:05 and credits the account. Based on RBI's RTGS FAQs, which of the following are correct?
I. Beta's bank had to credit the account by 21:35.
II. Beta's account statement must show Alpha Traders' name, and Alpha's statement must show Beta Ltd's name.
III. Alpha learns of the credit only by asking Beta, since banks do not confirm RTGS credits.

options.text: II and III only
I and III only
I, II and III
I and II only

solution.concept: Applying RTGS crediting and statement rules
solution.explanation: RTGS runs 24x7, and the beneficiary bank must credit within 30 minutes of receiving the message, so by 21:35. RBI requires members to show the ordering customer's name on the beneficiary's statement and the beneficiary's name on the originator's statement. Through positive confirmation, Beta's bank sends an acknowledgement of credit through RTGS/SFMS to Alpha's bank, which informs Alpha, so III is wrong.
steps: Statements carry the counterparty's name -> II correct
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with III are wrong because positive confirmation informs the remitter through its bank; 'II and III' and 'I and III' also omit a correct statement.
solution.final_answer: Option D: I and II only

fact_checks.claim: The beneficiary bank must credit the account within 30 minutes of receiving the message.

Members must show the debtor (ordering customer) name and creditor (beneficiary customer) name. The beneficiary's statement shows the originator's name, and the originator's statement shows the beneficiary's name.
The beneficiary bank sends a credit acknowledgement through RTGS/SFMS messaging to the remitting bank, which can then update its customer.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: An IMPS transfer debits the sender's account but the beneficiary's account is not credited. Under RBI's circular of 20 September 2019 on harmonisation of turn-around time (TAT) for failed transactions, by when must the beneficiary bank reverse it?

options.text: Within T + 5 days
Within 2 hours of the next settlement batch
Latest on T + 1 day, where T is the day of the transaction
Within 30 days, after the customer files a complaint

solution.explanation: RBI's 2019 framework on harmonisation of TAT says that when an IMPS transfer debits the account but the beneficiary is not credited, the beneficiary bank must auto-reverse it latest on T + 1 day. Beyond that, the bank pays ₹100 per day of delay to the customer.
steps: Failed IMPS credit -> auto-reversal by beneficiary bank
Deadline: T + 1 day; then ₹100 per day
solution.why_others_wrong: T + 5 applies to failures such as ATM cash not dispensed; the 2-hour rule belongs to NEFT; and the reversal is automatic, not dependent on a complaint.
solution.final_answer: Option C: Latest on T + 1 day, where T is the day of the transaction

fact_checks.claim: IMPS (row 3a, beneficiary not credited): Reversal by the beneficiary bank "latest on T + 1 day." Compensation is ₹100 per day beyond T + 1.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: In December 2024 RBI asked banks to offer a beneficiary account name look-up facility for RTGS and NEFT by 1 April 2025, noting that a similar check already existed in which systems, and asking which body to build it?

options.text: UPI and IMPS; IDRBT was advised to develop it on the SFMS platform
AePS and NACH; NPCI was advised to develop it and onboard all banks
UPI and IMPS; NPCI was advised to develop it and onboard all banks
Cheque truncation and NACH; CCIL was advised to develop it

solution.explanation: RBI's circular of 30 December 2024 notes that UPI and IMPS already let a remitter verify the beneficiary's name before paying, and extends a similar facility to RTGS and NEFT. NPCI was advised to develop the facility and onboard all banks; NPCI does not store any data relating to it.
steps: Existing name check: UPI and IMPS
solution.why_others_wrong: IDRBT and CCIL were not given this task; AePS, NACH and cheque truncation are not the systems RBI cited as already offering pre-payment name verification.
solution.final_answer: Option C: UPI and IMPS; NPCI was advised to develop it and onboard all banks

fact_checks.claim: UPI and IMPS already let a remitter check the beneficiary's name before paying ... "National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) has been advised to develop the facility and onboard all banks."
Direct and sub-members must offer the facility "no later than April 1, 2025." "NPCI shall not store any data relating to this facility."

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: On day T, Ravi's IMPS transfer debits his account but is never credited to the beneficiary; the reversal reaches his account on T + 4. On the same day T, an ATM of another bank debits his account without dispensing cash; that reversal is concluded on T + 7. Under RBI's circular of 20 September 2019 on harmonisation of TAT and customer compensation for failed transactions, what total compensation is due to Ravi?

solution.concept: Compensation for delayed reversal of failed transactions
solution.explanation: For an IMPS transfer not credited to the beneficiary, reversal is due latest on T + 1, and ₹100 per day is payable beyond that. For an ATM transaction where cash is not dispensed, reversal is due within T + 5, with ₹100 per day beyond. IMPS: 4 − 1 = 3 days × ₹100 = ₹300; ATM: 7 − 5 = 2 days × ₹100 = ₹200; total ₹500.
solution.why_others_wrong: ₹900 wrongly applies the T + 1 deadline to the ATM failure too; ₹1,100 counts delay from day T; ₹300 ignores the ATM compensation.
solution.final_answer: Option B: ₹500

fact_checks.claim: IMPS (row 3a, beneficiary not credited): Reversal by the beneficiary bank "latest on T + 1 day." Compensation is ₹100 per day beyond T + 1.
ATM (cash not dispensed, row 1a): "Pro-active reversal (R) of failed transaction within a maximum of T + 5 days." Compensation is ₹100 per day of delay beyond T + 5.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: In June 2022, RBI allowed credit cards to be linked to the UPI platform for the first time. Which credit cards were to be linked to begin with?

options.text: RuPay credit cards
Visa credit cards
Mastercard credit cards
Corporate credit cards of all networks

steps: UPI earlier linked only savings/current accounts
First credit cards on UPI: RuPay
solution.why_others_wrong: Visa, Mastercard and corporate cards were not the starting point; RBI specified RuPay credit cards to begin with.
solution.final_answer: Option A: RuPay credit cards

fact_checks.claim: "It is now proposed to allow linking of credit cards on the UPI platform." "To begin with, the Rupay credit cards will be linked to the UPI platform."

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: NPCI's National Automated Clearing House (NACH), used for bulk payments such as salaries, dividends and EMIs, was earlier available only on days when banks were functional. From which date did RBI decide, in June 2021, to make NACH available on all days of the week?

options.text: 1 July 2021
16 December 2019
14 December 2020
1 August 2021

solution.concept: NACH on all days of the week
solution.explanation: In its Statement on Developmental and Regulatory Policies of 4 June 2021, RBI noted that NACH was available only on bank working days and, to take advantage of RTGS being available on all days, decided to make NACH available on all days of the week throughout the year from 1 August 2021.
steps: Leveraging 24x7 RTGS -> NACH on all days from 1 August 2021

solution.final_answer: Option D: 1 August 2021

In the interest of customer convenience, and to take advantage of the availability of RTGS on all days of the year, it is proposed to make available NACH on all days of the week throughout the year, effective August 1, 2021.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: RBI's AePS Directions on due diligence of AePS Touchpoint Operators (ATOs), effective 1 January 2026, apply to the agents through whom customers withdraw cash using Aadhaar biometrics. Which requirement do they impose on acquiring banks?

options.text: KYC-based due diligence before onboarding an ATO, repeated for an ATO inactive for a continuous period of three months
Each ATO must be a permanent employee of the acquiring bank
Each ATO must be licensed directly by NPCI before onboarding
Each ATO must deposit a security of ₹1 lakh with UIDAI

solution.concept: Due diligence of AePS Touchpoint Operators
solution.explanation: RBI issued the final Directions on 27 June 2025, effective 1 January 2026, to curb AePS frauds. Acquiring banks must carry out KYC-based due diligence of ATOs before onboarding them, and the KYC verification applies again to ATOs that have remained inactive for a continuous period of three months. Banks must also monitor ATOs through their transaction monitoring systems.
solution.why_others_wrong: ATOs need not be bank employees (they can be BCs or sub-agents); NPCI does not license ATOs; and no UIDAI security deposit is prescribed.
solution.final_answer: Option A: KYC-based due diligence before onboarding an ATO, repeated for an ATO inactive for a continuous period of three months

fact_checks.claim: The directions cover due diligence requirements for ATOs and risk management instructions for their activities. "These directions shall come into effect from January 01, 2026."

Acquiring banks must "conduct due diligence as per the Know Your Customer (KYC) Directions, 2016" ... KYC verification applies to operators who "have remained inactive for a continuous period of three months".

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about RBI's circular of 22 August 2024 on processing of e-mandates for recurring transactions:
I. Auto-replenishment of FASTag and NCMC balances, as and when the balance falls below a threshold set by the customer, was brought under the e-mandate framework.
II. Such auto-replenishment debits are exempt from the requirement of a pre-debit notification at least 24 hours before the debit, because they are recurring but have no fixed periodicity.
III. For these payments, all other instructions of the e-mandate framework ceased to apply.
Which of the above is/are correct?

options.text: I only
II and III only
I and II only
I, II and III

solution.concept: E-mandates for FASTag and NCMC top-ups
solution.explanation: The circular included auto-replenishment of FASTag (NPCI's NETC tag) and the National Common Mobility Card in the e-mandate framework whenever the balance falls below a customer-set threshold (I). Since these payments recur without fixed periodicity, they are exempt from the 24-hour pre-debit notification (II). All other e-mandate instructions continue to apply, so III is wrong.
steps: I: FASTag/NCMC top-ups under e-mandates -> true
solution.why_others_wrong: Any option with III is wrong because the circular keeps the rest of the framework; 'I only' leaves out the pre-debit exemption in II.
solution.final_answer: Option C: I and II only

fact_checks.claim: It has been decided to include auto-replenishment of FASTag and NCMC, as and when the balance falls below a threshold ... Payments for auto-replenishment, since they are recurring in nature but without any fixed periodicity, will be exempt from the requirement of pre-debit notification

the issuer shall send a pre-debit notification to the customer at least 24 hours prior to the actual charge / debit ... All other instructions provided under the e-mandate framework shall continue to remain applicable.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Payments banks may issue prepaid payment instruments (PPIs) in addition to opening normal accounts. Under RBI's Payments Banks – Miscellaneous Directions, 2025, which restriction applies to the group to which a payments bank belongs?

options.text: No entity in the group may hold a banking licence of any kind for 10 years
The group must route all its UPI transactions through the payments bank
The group may hold a PPI entity only if it is listed on a stock exchange
A separate PPI-issuing entity cannot coexist with the payments bank in the same group

solution.explanation: The Directions say payments banks may undertake only restricted activities such as accepting demand deposits, and they can issue PPIs in addition to opening normal accounts. Because the payments bank itself can issue PPIs, a separate PPI entity cannot coexist with it in the same group.
steps: Hence no separate PPI entity in the same group
solution.why_others_wrong: The Directions impose no 10-year bar on other licences, no UPI-routing rule and no listing-based exception; they simply prohibit a PPI entity in the same group.
solution.final_answer: Option D: A separate PPI-issuing entity cannot coexist with the payments bank in the same group

fact_checks.claim: PBs may undertake only certain restricted activities such as acceptance of demand deposits ... PBs can issue PPIs in addition to opening normal accounts ... a PPI entity cannot coexist with the PB in the same group.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A payments bank both maintains savings accounts and issues prepaid wallets (PPIs) to its customers. Under RBI's Payments Banks – Miscellaneous Directions, 2025, how does the ₹2 lakh end-of-day limit per individual customer treat the customer's PPI balance with that payments bank?

options.text: The PPI balance is excluded and has a separate ₹2 lakh limit
The PPI balance also counts towards the ₹2 lakh limit
The PPI balance counts only if it exceeds ₹50,000
The PPI balance counts only for customers with minimum KYC

solution.concept: Scope of the payments bank balance limit
solution.explanation: Payments banks may hold a maximum balance of ₹2,00,000 per individual customer at the end of the day, and the Directions state that this individual customer limit applies to PPI balances also. So deposits and wallet balances with the payments bank are taken together.
steps: Limit: ₹2 lakh per individual customer at day-end
solution.why_others_wrong: There is no separate wallet limit within a payments bank, no ₹50,000 threshold and no KYC-based carve-out for counting PPI balances in this limit.
solution.final_answer: Option B: The PPI balance also counts towards the ₹2 lakh limit

fact_checks.claim: PBs are restricted to holding a maximum balance of ₹2,00,000 per individual customer at the end of the day. The individual customer limit applies to PPI balances also.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Payments banks are barred from lending. Under RBI's Payments Banks – Miscellaneous Directions, 2025, which exception to this bar exists?

options.text: Loans to its directors, if approved by the full Board without the interested director
Loans to its own employees out of the bank's own funds, under a Board-approved policy capping such loans
Overdrafts up to ₹10,000 to customers whose accounts have run satisfactorily for six months
Loans against the pledge of the customer's own fixed deposit with the payments bank

solution.explanation: The Directions say a payments bank shall not lend to any person, including its directors. The only carve-out is lending to its own employees out of the bank's own funds, as per a Board-approved policy that sets caps on such loans.
steps: General rule: no lending to any person, including directors
Exception: own employees, own funds, Board policy with caps
solution.why_others_wrong: Directors are expressly covered by the bar; the ₹10,000 overdraft is a PMJDY feature of full-service banks, not of payments banks; and payments banks cannot accept fixed deposits, so there is no deposit to lend against.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Loans to its own employees out of the bank's own funds, under a Board-approved policy capping such loans

fact_checks.claim: A bank shall not lend to any person including its directors ... the bank may lend to its own employees out of the bank's own funds ... a Board approved policy outlining the caps on such loans.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A payments bank collects a security deposit of ₹5 lakh from a technology vendor that provides it services. Under RBI's Payments Banks – Miscellaneous Directions, 2025, how is this treated against the ₹2 lakh end-of-day limit?

options.text: It is outside the limit, which applies to customer deposits and not to security or earnest money deposits
It breaches the limit, so ₹3 lakh must be swept to a partner bank at the end of the day
It is allowed only if the vendor is a scheduled commercial bank
It must be held in Treasury Bills, as payments banks cannot hold any balance above ₹2 lakh

solution.concept: What the payments bank limit covers
solution.explanation: The ₹2 lakh end-of-day cap is a limit per individual customer. The Directions clarify that it applies to customer deposits and not to any security or earnest money deposit, such as one collected from a service provider.
solution.why_others_wrong: A sweep applies only to customer balances above the limit; there is no condition that the vendor be a bank; and nothing requires such a deposit to be held in Treasury Bills.
solution.final_answer: Option A: It is outside the limit, which applies to customer deposits and not to security or earnest money deposits

fact_checks.claim: The above limit shall apply to customer deposits and not to any security/earnest money deposit

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A payments bank (PB) has a sweep arrangement under which its customers' balances above ₹2 lakh move to their accounts with a partner bank, for which it is also a business correspondent. Under RBI's Payments Banks – Miscellaneous Directions, 2025, consider: I. With a general consent from the customer, the PB may itself initiate debits in the customer's account held with the partner bank. II. As the partner bank's BC, the PB may facilitate withdrawals and transfers by the customer from that account. III. The PB may arrange intraday funding for the customer against the balance lying with the partner bank. Which of the above is/are correct?

options.text: I and II only
II and III only
II only
I, II and III

solution.concept: Limits of the payments bank sweep arrangement
solution.explanation: The PB shall not have rights to operate or real-time access to funds held with the other bank and shall not initiate any debit in the customer's account with another bank, even under a power of attorney or general consent (I wrong). As a BC of that bank it may facilitate withdrawals and transfers by the customer (II right). It shall neither arrange nor avail of intraday funding for customers based on balances with other banks (III wrong).

solution.why_others_wrong: Any option including I or III is wrong, because the Directions bar both self-initiated debits and intraday funding against the swept balances.
solution.final_answer: Option C: II only

fact_checks.claim: PBs shall not initiate any debit transactions in the customer's account, held with another bank ... However, as a BC of a bank, PBs may facilitate withdrawals and transfers by the customer
A PB shall neither arrange nor avail of intraday funding facilities for its customers

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: At the end of a day, Kiran, a small trader, has ₹1,40,000 in his savings account with a payments bank and ₹45,000 in a PPI wallet issued by the same payments bank. He has also placed an earnest money deposit of ₹50,000 with the payments bank as a service provider to it. Under RBI's Payments Banks – Miscellaneous Directions, 2025, what is the position?

Balance counted is ₹1,90,000; ₹10,000 of the earnest money counts towards the limit

Yes, after five years of operations with RBI's approval
No, small finance banks are not allowed to set up any subsidiaries
Yes, but only an NBFC subsidiary for microfinance

It may, because both banks would be held under an NOFHC
It may, if the SFB operates only in north-eastern States
It may, if the universal bank holds less than 26% of the SFB

questions.question_text: A small finance bank's total priority sector lending in the previous financial year was ₹6,000 crore. This year it lends to RBI-registered NBFC-MFIs (members of an RBI-recognised SRO, each with a gross loan portfolio below ₹500 crore as on 31 March of the previous year) for on-lending to individuals. Its eligible outstanding to them at the four quarter-ends was ₹520 crore, ₹560 crore, ₹640 crore and ₹680 crore. Under RBI's PSL Directions, 2025, how much of this lending can it classify as priority sector?

options.text: Only ₹520 crore, the lowest quarter-end figure, because the cap is tested at every quarter-end
None, because on-lending through NBFC-MFIs is not allowed for SFBs
Only up to ₹300 crore, because the cap is 5% of last year's PSL
All of it, as the four-quarter average of ₹600 crore is within the cap of 10% of last year's PSL

solution.concept: SFB lending to MFIs for on-lending
solution.explanation: SFBs may classify loans to registered NBFC-MFIs and other MFIs that are SRO members and have a gross loan portfolio of up to ₹500 crore (as on 31 March of the previous year) for on-lending to individuals. Such credit is capped at 10% of the bank's total PSL in the previous year (₹600 crore here), and adherence is measured by averaging across the four quarters: (520 + 560 + 640 + 680)/4 = ₹600 crore, which is within the cap.
solution.why_others_wrong: The cap is checked on the four-quarter average, not at each quarter-end; the general bar on NBFC on-lending does not cover this specific MFI route for SFBs; and the cap is 10%, not 5%.
solution.final_answer: Option D: All of it, as the four-quarter average of ₹600 crore is within the cap of 10% of last year's PSL

Four hours a day on at least five days a week
Three hours a day on at least four days a week
Eight hours a day on all working days

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A Business Correspondent (BC) company has been appointed by two banks. Under RBI's Commercial Banks – Branch Authorisation Directions, 2025, which statement is correct?

options.text: This is not allowed; a BC may work for only one bank
This is allowed, but at the point of customer interface each retail outlet or sub-agent represents the bank that appointed it
This is allowed only if both banks are public sector banks
This is allowed, and each outlet may offer both banks' products side by side as a common agent

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under RBI's Unique Identifiers in Financial Markets Directions, 2026, the Legal Entity Identifier (LEI) that parties to a financial transaction must hold is a unique identity code of how many characters?

It identifies each investor in mutual funds, has 10 characters and is the same as the PAN
It identifies each OTC derivative transaction, has a maximum of 52 characters and begins with the LEI of the generating entity
It identifies each government security, has 20 characters and is issued by CCIL

Structure: LEI of generating entity + unique code

Credit default swaps on government securities and State Development Loans
Permission for market-makers to sell credit default swaps to individuals
Credit derivatives on asset-backed and mortgage-backed securities

T-bills can be lent under GSL, but cannot be placed as collateral
T-bills can neither be lent nor placed as collateral under GSL

A scheduled commercial bank with a minimum net worth of ₹500 crore

Any foreign entity registered with IOSCO, with no net worth requirement

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A resident company with a net worth of ₹400 crore and turnover of ₹900 crore (latest audited) holds ₹40 crore face value of a rated corporate bond. It is a retail user; it may buy the full ₹50 crore as long as it holds the bond
It is a retail user and is not allowed to buy CDS protection at all
It is a retail user; it may buy protection only to hedge, for a notional of at most ₹40 crore

A secured instrument, with a tenor of 7 days to 90 days
A secured instrument, with a tenor of 90 days to one year
An unsecured instrument, with a tenor of one year to three years

steps: Tenor: 90 days to 1 year (CP: 7 days to 1 year)

solution.final_answer: Option C: A secured instrument, with a tenor of 90 days to one year

questions.question_text: A company issued a 91-day Commercial Paper on 1 September 2026. Its cash position improves and it wants to buy back the CP from investors on 5 September 2026. Under RBI's CP Directions, 2024, which statement is correct?

options.text: It can buy back on 5 September from any investors it chooses, at par value
It cannot buy back the CP at all before maturity
It can buy back on 5 September only with SEBI's prior approval, and may resell the CP later

It cannot buy back on 5 September, as a CP may be bought back only after 7 days from issue; any later buyback must be offered to all investors on identical terms at the prevailing market price, and the CP extinguished

solution.explanation: An issuer may buy back CP before maturity only after seven days from issue (NCDs only after 90 days). The offer must be made to all investors in that issue on identical terms, at the prevailing market price, and the bought-back CP is extinguished on the buyback date. 5 September is only four days after issue, so the buyback is not allowed then.
steps: Issue 1 Sep -> 5 Sep is 4 days later (< 7 days)
Later buyback: all investors, identical terms, market price, extinguished
solution.why_others_wrong: Selective buyback at par is not allowed; buyback is permitted after 7 days, not barred entirely; SEBI approval and resale of bought-back CP have no basis, as the CP must be extinguished.
solution.final_answer: Option D: It cannot buy back on 5 September, as a CP may be bought back only after 7 days from issue; any later buyback must be offered to all investors on identical terms at the prevailing market price, and the CP extinguished

fact_checks.claim: CPs can be bought back only after 7 days from issue, and NCDs only after 90 days. The offer must go to all investors on identical terms, at the prevailing market price. Bought-back instruments are extinguished on the buyback date.

solution.final_answer: Option B: ₹96.49; 500 units

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: In September 2026 SEBI's Board amended Regulation 62A of the LODR Regulations for issuers listing non-convertible debentures (NCDs) for the first time. What changed?

All unlisted NCDs issued since 2015 must now be listed within three months
NCDs may no longer be issued on a private placement basis by listed entities
Such an issuer need no longer list all its outstanding unlisted NCDs; only prospective NCD issuances must be listed

New: only prospective issuances need listing

At least 75% in equity, with at least 25% each in large cap, mid cap and small cap companies

AMFI must individually approve each sectoral/thematic scheme before its NFO
AMFI sets the maximum expense ratio of each sectoral/thematic scheme every quarter
AMFI computes the portfolio overlap of each scheme and publishes it monthly

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A banking sectoral fund (Scheme A) holds stocks P 20%, Q 15%, R 25%, S 10% and T 30%. The same AMC's flexi cap fund (Scheme B) holds P 10%, Q 25%, R 20%, U 30% and V 15%. Using SEBI's portfolio overlap methodology of February 2026, what is the overlap, and does it meet the limit for sectoral/thematic schemes?

options.text: 60%, breaching the 50% limit
57.5%, breaching the 50% limit
55%, breaching the 50% limit
45%, within the 50% limit

solution.explanation: Overlap is the sum, over common stocks only, of the lower of the two weights: P min(20,10) = 10, Q min(15,25) = 15, R min(25,20) = 20; S, T, U and V count zero. Total = 45%. A sectoral/thematic scheme may overlap no more than 50% with other equity schemes (except large cap schemes), so 45% is within the limit.

solution.final_answer: Option D: 45%, within the 50% limit

questions.question_text: The Economic Survey 2025-26 noted that the Centre's capital expenditure rose from ₹2.63 lakh crore in FY18 to ₹11.21 lakh crore in FY26 (BE). Over these eight years, at roughly what compound annual growth rate (CAGR) did central capex grow?

options.text: About 17.5% a year
About 41% a year
About 23% a year
About 20% a year

solution.concept: Growth of public capex; compound annual growth rate
solution.explanation: The multiple is 11.21 ÷ 2.63 ≈ 4.26 (the Survey calls it a rise of 4.2 times). FY18 to FY26 is 8 years, so CAGR = 4.26^(1/8) − 1 ≈ 0.199, i.e. about 20% a year (check: 1.2^8 ≈ 4.3).
solution.shortcut: Test round rates: 1.2^2 = 1.44, 1.2^4 ≈ 2.07, 1.2^8 ≈ 4.3, which matches the 4.26 multiple.
solution.why_others_wrong: 17.5% spreads the growth over 9 years and 23% over 7; 41% is a simple average (326% ÷ 8) that ignores compounding.
solution.final_answer: Option D: About 20% a year

options.text: The minimum period of contribution is 20 years or more, and a subscriber may exit voluntarily before 60 on deduction of the Government co-contribution and the return on it
The minimum period of contribution is 10 years, and a subscriber who exits voluntarily before 60 gets the full corpus including the Government co-contribution
The minimum period of contribution is 20 years or more, and voluntary exit before 60 is not permitted in any case
The minimum period of contribution is 15 years, and a subscriber may exit voluntarily before 60 on forfeiting all contributions

solution.concept: APY contribution period and voluntary exit
solution.explanation: Pension under APY begins at 60 and the latest joining age is 40, so every subscriber contributes for at least 20 years. Voluntary exit allowed; Government co-contribution and its return deducted

questions.question_text: Two students secure merit admission to Quality Higher Educational Institutions and take PM Vidyalaxmi education loans; neither gets any other scholarship or subvention. A borrows ₹7 lakh and her annual family income is ₹9 lakh. B borrows ₹12 lakh and his family income is ₹6 lakh. Which statement is correct?

options.text: A's loan gets the guarantee and 3% subvention; B gets subvention of ₹36,000 a year during the moratorium
A's loan gets neither benefit; B's loan gets the 75% guarantee and subvention of ₹30,000 a year
A's loan gets the 75% guarantee but no subvention; B's loan gets no guarantee but subvention of ₹30,000 a year during the moratorium
A's loan gets the 75% guarantee but no subvention; B gets the guarantee on ₹7.5 lakh and subvention of ₹36,000 a year

solution.concept: PM Vidyalaxmi: guarantee and interest subvention
solution.explanation: The 75% guarantee is for loans up to ₹7.5 lakh, so A (₹7 lakh) is covered and B (₹12 lakh) is not. The 3% subvention is for family income up to ₹8 lakh and on loans up to ₹10 lakh (only the first ₹10 lakh of a bigger loan), during the moratorium: A (₹9 lakh income) gets none; B gets 3% × ₹10 lakh = ₹30,000 a year.
steps: Guarantee: A yes (≤ ₹7.5 lakh), B no
solution.why_others_wrong: ₹36,000 applies 3% to the whole ₹12 lakh; B's loan exceeds the ₹7.5 lakh guarantee limit; A qualifies for the guarantee.
solution.final_answer: Option C: A's loan gets the 75% guarantee but no subvention; B's loan gets no guarantee but subvention of ₹30,000 a year during the moratorium
